subject: Follow-up: Data boundary confirmation & ops checklist
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@fintrust.com>, James O'Neil <james.oneil@fintrust.com>
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 20 Nov 2027 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: Data boundary confirmation & ops checklist

Hi Elena / James —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Wanted to capture the key takeaways and proposed next steps so we have a shared ops checklist: 

Summary of needs you raised:
- Strong tenant/data isolation between FinTrust and other customers (regulatory requirement).
- Preference for private networking (VPC peering or customer-managed VPC) and options to avoid egress through shared infra.
- Customer-managed keys (bring-your-own KMS) and strict access controls for key material.
- Audit log retention for 7 years and SOC2 evidence for control verification.
- Low-latency path for on-prem connectors (hybrid inference) for some workloads.

Where Redwood fits (high level):
- Hosted API: fastest to ship, but not suitable given your isolation & KMS needs.
- Dedicated: reserved, Redwoods-managed GPU pools with tenant isolation at the workload layer; good for predictable throughput and stronger data controls, but control plane remains Redwood-managed.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): full network isolation — private control plane or customer-managed VPC, support for private endpoints, and options for on-prem connectors. Best fit when customers require isolated networking and full control of keys and routing.

Evidence / artifacts we can provide (next 48–72h):
1) SOC2 Type II report (redacted) and pen-test summary.
2) KMS integration notes and encryption whitepaper (how CMK is supported).
3) Network diagram templates showing VPC peering, private endpoints, and firewall rules.
4) Draft mutual action plan (MAP) — procurement timeline + Egress/Ingress SLAs.

Proposed next steps:
- We’ll send the items above -> ETA Tue 11/23. (I’m attaching a short list of questions we have so we can tailor the VPC proposal.)
- Technical deep-dive call with your infra/security team next week to validate network flows and KMS requirements. Can you confirm availability for Tue 11/24 or Wed 11/25 (mornings PT)?
- Procurement: if Private VPC is required, we’ll need your legal/procurement to review the MAP; I can include our security checklist for legal to triage.

Attached: FinTrust_Security_Questions.pdf (your questionnaire), mutual-action-plan.docx (draft placeholder).

Thanks — happy to slot the deep-dive once you confirm a time.

— Diego Fernandez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
diego.fernandez@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0126

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@fintrust.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: James O'Neil <james.oneil@fintrust.com>, security@fintrust.com
Date: Sat, 20 Nov 2027 16:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Data boundary confirmation & ops checklist

Diego —

Thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side so you can scope the MAP correctly: 

1) By "data isolation" we mean both logical and physical separation where possible. Priority order: Private VPC with customer-managed control plane > Private VPC with Redwood control plane but customer-only workloads > Dedicated nodes with strict tenancy controls.
2) KMS: we require full BYOK support. Keys must be customer-owned and stored in our KMS (AWS KMS). We need to understand how key rotation and rekeying works across the inference runtime.
3) Audit logs: we will want read-only access to raw audit logs (S3) and the ability to push logs into our SIEM. Retention requirement: 7 years for specific endpoints.
4) Network: For low-latency on-prem connectors, we prefer a model where inference traffic can stay on our private WAN (no public egress). Can you confirm options for private peering or direct connect?

I’ve attached our initial security questionnaire (FinTrust_Security_Questions.pdf). James (procurement) is copied — he’ll track contract timeline. 

Availability: Tue 11/24 morning PT works for our infra/security folks.

— Elena
Head of Information Security | FinTrust
elena.ruiz@fintrust.com

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@fintrust.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 20 Nov 2027 17:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Data boundary confirmation & ops checklist

Elena —

Thanks for the specifics — wanted to address each bullet so your team can decide between Dedicated and Private without ambiguity.

KMS / CMK:
- Redwood supports AWS KMS CMKs in Private VPC deployments and in our Private (air-gapped) on-prem packages. For Dedicated we support envelope encryption where key material can be customer-provided; however, Dedicated’s control plane is Redwood-managed so there are additional controls to review. I’ll attach the encryption flow diagram.

Audit logs / retention:
- We can stream raw audit logs to an S3 bucket you own (recommended) and provide read-only roles. Retention policy can be configured via lifecycle rules on your bucket to meet the 7-year requirement. We also support pushing events to Splunk/Datadog via Kinesis.

Network / private peering:
- Private VPC: options include VPC peering, PrivateLink endpoints, or AWS Direct Connect. All avoid public egress.
- Dedicated (Redwood-managed): supports IP allowlisting and private peering for control-plane API calls, but some telemetry may route through Redwood-managed aggregation points unless you choose the Private control plane deployment.

Operational notes: 
- Private control plane (customer VPC): full isolation, customer controls control-plane networking and KMS. This is the strongest option but requires slightly higher setup time and a managed ops window for upgrades.
- Dedicated capacity (reserved capacity): faster provisioning, predictable throughput, and can be configured to meet many compliance requirements — tradeoff is the control plane remains with Redwood.

Artifacts I’ll send (in this thread): encryption-whitepaper.pdf, network-flows-diagram.png, SOC2-redacted.pdf. I can also prepare a short matrix that maps each FinTrust requirement to the minimum deployment mode and outstanding open actions.

Suggested immediate next steps:
1) Tech deep-dive Tue 11/24 09:30 PT — link to invite will be sent after Diego confirms.
2) I’ll draft a Deployment Decision Matrix and share by EOD Mon 11/23.
3) Procurement: Diego, please include James on the MAP and confirm procurement milestones for Private control plane (if chosen).

— Sergio Alvarez
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai

Elena / James —

Appreciate the quick replies and the questionnaire. Confirming we’ll do the technical deep-dive Tue 11/24 @ 09:30 PT. Sergio will send the invite and proposed agenda (network flows, KMS, audit log handoff).

Next items for procurement thread:

- James — once you review the MAP I’ll loop in legal to start redlines. If FinTrust prefers Private, we’ll prepare a scoped SOW and a support/upgrade window plan.

DocuSign: I’m including a placeholder MAP link below — once we agree on mode and timeline we’ll push an official DocuSign. https://docusign.com/FT-FT-2027-019-MAP
